title: Clean Architecture in Ruby
intro: Senior Ruby interviews at product companies often ask about moving beyond Rails conventions to more explicit architectures. Hexagonal architecture in Ruby uses duck-typed interfaces (Ruby Protocols via respond_to?) as ports and plain Ruby objects as adapters, keeping the domain layer free from Rails specifics. The dry-rb ecosystem — dry-validation, dry-types, dry-monads, dry-transaction — provides type safety and explicit error handling in a language that otherwise has neither. DDD in Ruby is less common than in Java but still appears at domain-heavy companies. This page covers the practical trade-offs: Rails' ActiveRecord-as-domain-model is fast to build and hard to test in isolation; hexagonal is slower to build and significantly easier to test at the unit level. The interview answer requires knowing both sides.
